\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Simple}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Simple
\section{Overview}

This module develops the ``simple'' hypercontractivity results for real-valued
Boolean functions $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, that is, the results obtainable by
direct induction on coordinates without the full general machinery. It builds up
the $(2,4)$, $(4/3,2)$, $(2,2k)$, and $(p,2)$ hypercontractivity inequalities for
the noise operator $T_\rho$, together with the supporting character, cardinality,
Fourier, and combinatorial lemmas used along the way.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Walsh character is unchanged by appending an unused coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_castSucc}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_castSucc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.chiS}
\difficulty{1}
Fix $n\in\bbn$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $b\in\{0,1\}$. Form the
point $(x,b)\in\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending $b$ as the final coordinate, and
regard $S$ as a subset $S'\subseteq[n+1]$ via the inclusion $[n]\hookrightarrow[n+1]$
that leaves each index fixed (so the new last coordinate never lies in $S'$). Then the
Walsh--Fourier character of $S'$ evaluated at the extended point agrees with that of $S$
at the original point:
\[
  \chi_{S'}\big((x,b)\big) \;=\; \chi_S(x).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Walsh character on an extended coordinate set]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_with_last}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_with_last}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq [n]$, let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, and let $b$ be a bit. Write $(x,b) \in
\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ for the point obtained by appending $b$ as the final coordinate, and let
$S' \subseteq [n+1]$ be the image of $S$ under the inclusion $[n] \hookrightarrow [n+1]$
of the first $n$ coordinates, together with the new last coordinate $n+1$. Then
\[
  \chi_{S'}(x,b) \;=\; \sigma(b)\,\chi_S(x),
\]
where $\sigma$ is the sign encoding; that is, adjoining the last coordinate to the
lifted index set multiplies the Walsh character by the sign of $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting a subset-sum by the last coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.finset_fin_succ_sum_partition}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.finset_fin_succ_sum_partition}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Fix $n \in \bbn$ and identify a subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ that omits the top
element $n$ with the corresponding subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, via the inclusion
$\iota$ that sends $T \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-1\}$ to the same set regarded inside
$\{0,\dots,n\}$. Then for every function $\varphi$ assigning a real number to each
subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$,
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n\}} \varphi(S)
  = \sum_{T \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-1\}} \varphi\bigl(\iota(T)\bigr)
  + \sum_{T \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-1\}} \varphi\bigl(\iota(T) \cup \{n\}\bigr),
\]
the two terms collecting the subsets of $\{0,\dots,n\}$ that exclude and that include
the element $n$, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality is preserved under the successor inclusion]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ be a finite set of indices, and let $\iota \colon
\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\} \hookrightarrow \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ be the order-preserving
inclusion that regards each index as an element of the enlarged range. Then the image
$\iota(S)$ has the same cardinality as $S$, that is, $\abs{\iota(S)} = \abs{S}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality after lifting a set and adjoining the top coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc_union_last}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc_union_last}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. Embed $S$ into
$\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ by the map that sends each index to itself, and adjoin the top
index $n$. Since $n$ is not the image of any element of $S$, this union satisfies
\[
\abs{\{\, i : i \in S \,\} \cup \{n\}} = \abs{S} + 1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise operator splits along the last coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc}
\leanok
\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.fourierCoeff_avgLast, Bonami.fourierCoeff_diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc, SimpleHypercontractivity.card_image_castSucc_union_last, SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_castSucc, SimpleHypercontractivity.chiS_snoc_with_last, SimpleHypercontractivity.finset_fin_succ_sum_partition}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $\rho \in \bbr$ and a Boolean function $f \colon \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, and let
$Af$ and $Df$ be the average and the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate,
each a Boolean function on $\{0,1\}^n$. For every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and every bit $b$,
\[
  T_\rho f(x, b) \;=\; T_\rho(Af)(x) \;+\; \sigma(b)\,\rho\,T_\rho(Df)(x),
\]
where $(x,b) \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}$ is the point obtained by appending $b$ as the last
coordinate, $\sigma$ is the sign encoding, and $T_\rho$ is the noise operator.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourth-moment decomposition under the noise operator]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.fourth_moment_noise_decomp}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.fourth_moment_noise_decomp}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p007-b004}
\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.fourth_moment_decomp, Bonami.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $\rho\in\bbr$. Write $g$ for
the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $h$ for the corresponding
half-difference, so that
\[
  g(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)+f(x,1)\bigr),\qquad
  h(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)-f(x,1)\bigr)
\]
are Boolean functions of the first $n$ variables. Then the fourth moment of $T_\rho f$
under the uniform measure decomposes as
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^4\bigr]
  = \E\bigl[(T_\rho g)^4\bigr]
  + 6\rho^2\,\E\bigl[(T_\rho g)^2\,(T_\rho h)^2\bigr]
  + \rho^4\,\E\bigl[(T_\rho h)^4\bigr].
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.expect_cs_sq, Bonami.expect_fourth_nonneg, Bonami.expect_sq_nonneg, Bonami.second_moment_decomp, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, SimpleHypercontractivity.fourth_moment_noise_decomp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $\rho\in\bbr$ be a noise
parameter satisfying $\rho^2\le 1/3$. Then the fourth moment of the noised function is
controlled by the square of its second moment:
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^4\bigr]\;\le\;\bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2,
\]
where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator and $\E$ denotes expectation under the uniform
measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Equivalently, $\norm{T_\rho f}_4\le\norm{f}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Hölder's inequality for the exponents $4/3$ and $4$]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_le_L43_L4}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_le_L43_L4}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, and take all expectations with
respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then their $L^2$ inner product satisfies
\[
  \langle f, g \rangle
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^{4/3}\,]\bigr)^{3/4}\,
  \bigl(\E[\,\abs{g}^{4}\,]\bigr)^{1/4}.
\]
\end{lemma}

  {SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_le_L43_L4}
  {context}

  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p008-b002}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_4, SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_le_L43_L4}
\difficulty{5}
For every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, applying the noise operator with
parameter $\rho=1/\sqrt3$ contracts the $L^2$ norm below the $L^{4/3}$ norm of the
original function:
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[(T_{1/\sqrt3} f)^2\bigr]\bigr)^{1/2}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{4/3}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{3/4},
\]
where both expectations are taken under the uniform measure on the hypercube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier expansion of the squared norm of a noised function]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n\in\bbn$, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let
$\rho\in\bbr$. Write $T_\rho$ for the noise operator with parameter $\rho$,
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ for the $L^2$ inner product under the uniform
measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, and $\hat f(S)$ for the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $f$ at
frequency $S\subseteq[n]$. Then
\[
  \langle T_\rho f,\, T_\rho f\rangle
  \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \bigl(\rho^{|S|}\bigr)^2\,\hat f(S)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Contractivity of the noise operator in $L^2$]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.contractivity}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.contractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $n$, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be any Boolean function, and let $\rho\in\bbr$
satisfy $\rho^2\le 1$. Writing $T_\rho$ for the noise operator, so that $T_\rho
f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$, one has
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big]\;\le\;\E\big[f^2\big],
\]
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[A bound on even binomial coefficients]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For every natural number $k \ge 1$ and every natural number $j$ with $j \le k$, the
inequality
\[
  \binom{2k}{2j} \;\le\; \binom{k}{j}\,(2k-1)^{j}
\]
holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$q$-th moment decomposition along the last coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp}
\leanok
\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.sum_boolCube_succ, Bonami.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $q$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function.
Write $g$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $h$ for the
half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, both Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$.
Then the $q$-th moment of $f$ under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ decomposes as
\[
  \E[f^q] \;=\; \E\!\left[\frac{(g+h)^q + (g-h)^q}{2}\right],
\]
where the expectation on the right is taken over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Moment decomposition of the noise operator across the last coordinate]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp}
\leanok
\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc, SimpleHypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $q$ be a
nonnegative integer. Write $A$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $D$
for the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, both functions on $\{0,1\}^n$.
Then the $q$-th moment of $T_\rho f$ over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
decomposes as
\[
  \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n+1}}\!\bigl[(T_\rho f)(x)^q\bigr]
= \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}\!\left[\frac{\bigl(T_\rho A(x) + \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q} +
\bigl(T_\rho A(x) - \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q}}{2}\right],
\]
where on the right-hand side the noise operator acts on functions of $n$ variables.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[$(2, 2k)$-hypercontractivity for the noise operator]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003
}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
\uses{Bonami.avgLast, Bonami.diffLast, Bonami.expect_sq_nonneg, Bonami.second_moment_decomp, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion, SimpleHypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq, SimpleHypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp}
\difficulty{7}
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a real number $\rho$ with $\rho^2 \le \dfrac{1}{2k-1}$.
Then for every function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ on the Boolean hypercube,
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^{2k}\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{k},
\]
where the expectation is taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$ and $T_\rho$ is
the noise operator $T_\rho f = \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S$.
Equivalently, $\norm{T_\rho f}_{2k} \le \norm{f}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$(2,q)$-hypercontractivity for even exponents]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\difficulty{3}
Let $q \ge 2$ be an even integer, and let $\rho \in \bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2 \le
\tfrac{1}{q-1}$. Then for every Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the noise
operator $T_\rho$ contracts from $L^2$ to $L^q$ in the sense that
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^q\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{q/2},
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$L^2$ contractivity of the noise operator]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.contractivity}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2\le 1$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean
function. Then the noise operator $T_\rho$ does not increase the $L^2$ norm under the
uniform measure:
\[
  \E\!\left[(T_\rho f)^2\right] \;\le\; \E\!\left[f^2\right].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A $(2,6)$-hypercontractive inequality for the noise operator]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_6}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007
}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_6}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b005,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p015-b003
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2\le \tfrac15$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be any
Boolean function. Then the sixth moment of the noised function $T_\rho f$ is controlled
by the cube of the second moment of $f$:
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^6\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^3,
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$(2,2k)$-hypercontractivity in norm form]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k_rpow}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003
}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k_rpow}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
\uses{Bonami.expect_sq_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, SimpleHypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\difficulty{3}
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a real noise rate $\rho$ satisfying $\rho^2 \le
\tfrac{1}{2k-1}$. Then for every Boolean function $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, the image
$T_\rho f$ under the noise operator obeys the $L^{2k}$-to-$L^2$ hypercontractive bound
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^{2k}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/(2k)} \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{1/2},
\]
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Self inner product equals expected square]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_expect_sq}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_expect_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{2}
For a Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the $L^2$ inner product of $f$ with
itself equals the expectation of its square: $\langle f, f\rangle = \E[f^2]$, that is,
$2^{-n}\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the expected square of a smoothed Boolean function]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $\rho\in\bbr$ be arbitrary.
Applying the noise operator $T_\rho$ to $f$ and averaging the square over the uniform
measure gives a nonnegative quantity:
\[
  \E\!\left[(T_\rho f)^2\right]\;\ge\;0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of an expected absolute power]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $p\in\bbr$ be any real exponent.
Then, under the uniform measure on the hypercube, the expected value of $\abs{f}^p$ is
nonnegative:
\[
\E\!\left[\,\abs{f}^{\,p}\,\right]\;=\;2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\abs{f(x)}^{\,p}\;\ge\;0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition of noise operators]
\lean{SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose}
\label{SimpleHypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier}
\difficulty{2}
For any real parameters $\rho,\sigma$ and any Boolean function
$f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, applying the noise operator $T_\sigma$ and then the noise
operator $T_\rho$ is the same as applying the single noise operator $T_{\rho\sigma}$;
that is,
\[
  T_\rho\bigl(T_\sigma f\bigr) \;=\; T_{\rho\sigma}\,f .
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint, SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, SimpleHypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg, SimpleHypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_expect_sq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $1 < p$ and $q \ge 2$ be conjugate exponents, so that $1/p + 1/q = 1$, let $\rho \in
\bbr$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function; write $\norm{g}_r =
(\E[\abs{g}^r])^{1/r}$ for the $L^r$ norm under the uniform measure on the hypercube.
Suppose Hölder's inequality holds for the exponent pair $(p,q)$, that is, $\langle u,
v\rangle \le \norm{u}_p\,\norm{v}_q$ for all Boolean functions $u,v$, and suppose the
noise operator satisfies the $(2,q)$ bound $\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho g}^q\bigr] \le
\bigl(\E[g^2]\bigr)^{q/2}$ for every Boolean function $g$. Then $T_\rho$ satisfies the
dual $(p,2)$ bound
\[
  \bigl(\E[(T_\rho f)^2]\bigr)^{1/2} \le \bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^p\,]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

Let $a,b,A,B,C,\rho$ be real numbers with $a\ge 0$, $b\ge 0$, and $B\ge 0$, and suppose
that $A\le a^2$, $B\le b^2$, $C^2\le AB$, and $\rho^2\le \tfrac13$. Then
\[
  A + 6\rho^2 C + \rho^4 B \;\le\; (a+b)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}
